definitions.explanation: A rapid exchange of words, lines, or musical phrases between two parties—a comedy duo's banter, the call-and-response of a festival chant, or the give-and-take in a negotiation. Emphasizes rhythm and reaction more than the literal content of what is said.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{掛|か}け{合|あ}い⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{面白|おもしろ}い→面白い：00589_omoshiroi⟧。
examples.english: The banter between the two of them is funny.

examples.japanese: ⟦{漫才|まんざい}→漫才：04458_manzai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{魅力|みりょく}→魅力：03749_miryoku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦テンポ→テンポ：04749_tenpo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧よい{掛|か}け{合|あ}いだ。
examples.english: The appeal of manzai lies in its well-paced banter.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{太鼓|たいこ}→太鼓：04049_taiko⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{笛|ふえ}→笛：03593_fue⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{掛|か}け{合|あ}い⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{観客|かんきゃく}→観客：02556_kankyaku⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{盛|も}り{上|あ}げた→盛り上げる：07895_moriageru⟧。
examples.english: At the festival, the call-and-response between the drums and flutes excited the audience.

notes:
Noun form of ⟦{掛|か}け{合|あ}う→掛け合う：05742_kakeau⟧ (to exchange back-and-forth). Used in entertainment, music, daily conversation, and even business contexts to describe lively two-way exchanges.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦テンポ→テンポ：04749_tenpo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧よい{掛|か}け{合|あ}い: well-paced banter
- {掛|か}け{合|あ}い⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{面白|おもしろ}さ: the appeal of the banter
- ⟦{息|いき}→息：02176_iki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{合|あ}った→合う：10466_au⟧{掛|か}け{合|あ}い: in-sync banter (the two parties are well-attuned)
- ⟦{歌|うた}→歌：02179_uta⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{掛|か}け{合|あ}い: a call-and-response in song

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{会話|かいわ}→会話：01271_kaiwa⟧: conversation — broader; no implication of rhythm or repartee
- ⟦やり{取|と}り→やり取り：07702_yaritori⟧: exchange — more about substance (of emails, messages) than rhythm
